title: Using thirty five squared, how do we find thirty six squared?
description: The video finds thirty six squared from thirty five squared by adding the next odd number, without multiplying. Keeko doubts the answer after adding thirty six, the new row, instead of the odd number.
teaching_notes: One idea: the next square is the old square plus the next odd number, and the nth odd number is two times n minus one. Watch for students who add the new side length instead of the next odd number.

video_script.why: The child sees that going from one square to the next adds an L-shaped strip, which is the next odd number.
video_script.substitution: Find the next odd number as two times the position minus one, and add it to the known square.
video_script.anchor: a square of side thirty five with an L-shaped strip beside it
video_script.wrong_answer: one thousand two hundred sixty one
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds thirty six, the new side, to 1225 and gets 1261. The new strip is an L with 35 + 35 + 1 = 71 unit squares, because the corner is counted once.
video_script.payoff_line: Thirty six squared is one thousand two hundred ninety six

final_answer.spoken: thirty six squared is one thousand two hundred ninety six

never_show: the numbers 125, 126 and 251 of the exercise videos
maths_rules: 35² is the sum of the first 35 odd numbers, and 36² is the sum of the first 36 odd numbers
the nth odd number is 2n − 1; the 36th is 2 × 36 − 1 = 72 − 1 = 71
the slip: 1225 + 36 = 1261 adds the new side; the L has 35 + 35 + 1 = 71
video_script.design: One idea: the next square adds the next odd number as an L. Wrong idea: adding the new side. The big square and its L stay in the anchor band.

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step one, thirty five squared is the sum of the first thirty five odd numbers.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Thirty six squared adds one more odd number, the thirty sixth.

beats.on_screen: the nth odd number is 2n − 1; the 36th is 2 × 36 − 1 = 71

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, to get an odd number, double its place and take away one.
<bookmark mark='seventyone'/>Double thirty six is seventy two, and one less is seventy one.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add seventy one to one thousand two hundred twenty five. That gives one thousand two hundred ninety six.

marks.six: 6 × 36 = 216 is written and the two parts are added to 1296

narration: <bookmark mark='thirty'/>Step four, check by multiplying. Thirty times thirty six is one thousand eighty.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Six times thirty six is two hundred sixteen, and together they make one thousand two hundred ninety six.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Thirty six squared is one thousand two hundred ninety six.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is one thousand two hundred sixty one, after adding thirty six.
<bookmark mark='ell'/>But the new strip is an L. It has thirty five on one side, thirty five on the other, and one corner.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>That is seventy one, the odd number we added.
